_comment: SparkUser, shipped by MintPlayer.Spark.Authorization (composition D6). Every application that
references the library has this type; none keeps a copy. An application changes it with a DELTA
file of the same name in its own App_Data/Model: persistentObject.name plus only what differs,
never an id (QnA's SparkUser.json shows UserName on the form only).
HAND-AUTHORED. The ids are UUIDv5 of 'authorization:SparkUser[.attributes.<Name>]' (D5), verified
by the generator (SPARK045); 'npm run stamp:library-model-ids -- libs/authorization/MintPlayer.Spark.Authorization'
writes them.
It exists so that a reference to a user (ApiToken.CreatedByUserId, a post's CreatedBy) renders the
user name instead of a raw document id: a reference resolves its label through the target type's
breadcrumb, and with no model at all BreadcrumbResolver falls back to the id string.
⚠️ Nothing may be added here without asking what it discloses. SparkUserActions declares no row
rule -- RowSecurity treats a missing rule as allowed -- so any attribute here is readable by anyone
who can read an object that references the user. Only UserName is declared: an attribute that is
not in the model cannot reach the wire, so credential material (PasswordHash, SecurityStamp,
tokens, ...) never can. UserName never contains '@' (the framework refuses it), so this label never
shows an email address; Email and PhoneNumber are deliberately absent.
⚠️ The synchronizer must never generate this type: it discovers properties by reflection and would
emit every credential field as a writable attribute. That is why it is hand-authored here.
⚠️ The breadcrumb names UserName (capital N). A placeholder that matches no attribute renders blank
rather than raising an error, so a typo here is silent.
